description:
Review baseline: release/3.0 at fb5b59bda429b7545f82072dabe10f8b299432dc.
Classification: upstream dependency finding with Connect follow-up.

Source task: 01a09c57-2619-7251-b3f3-113072d196ce

- **P1 — ExMCP accepts a broader notification filter from the server.**  
  [ExMCP subscription.ex:157](/var/folders/8l/nyn2qp4d441b1zrgypxgry7m0000gn/T/connect-mcp-review-dmjzx4fq/ex_mcp_1_3_0/lib/ex_mcp/client/subscription.ex:157)

  The locked ExMCP package accepted an acknowledgment that added an unrequested private resource. On reconnect, it uses that acknowledged filter for automatic resource reads. Connect authorizes the requested filter, then forwards the resulting snapshot.

  **Correction:** ExMCP must reject acknowledgments that expand the requested filter before it starts automatic reads. Keep protocol handling in ExMCP. Connect must retain and enforce its authorized scope.

Acceptance: Reproduce the reported case against current source, apply the smallest correction described above, and add focused verification of both the failing case and supported behavior. For documentation/design work, update the public contract and verify its examples/callers. Preserve tenant, scope, lease, and host ownership boundaries. Use fresh matching v3 dependencies for final verification; saved local v2 build artifacts do not establish v3 conformance.

Do not modify jido_mcp or publish packages. Full source review and its coverage/verification limits are preserved in the parent epic comments.

comments.text: Submitted upstream defect: https://github.com/azmaveth/ex_mcp/issues/42 . Connect tracking: https://github.com/agentjido/jido_connect/issues/82 . Both issues are linked. Upstream owns filter acknowledgment validation; Connect must retain authorized scope and verify the fixed dependency with integration tests. No code changes or publication.

Prepared upstream fix in ExMCP PR https://github.com/azmaveth/ex_mcp/pull/46 . Connect adoption remains open until ExMCP releases the acknowledgment validation and Connect verifies that reconnect reads stay within authorized scope.

Connect defense landed in 44736e54 on release/3.0. The session now keeps its authorized filter, drops out-of-scope events, and stops before forwarding a broadened reconnect snapshot. The focused MCP test reproduced the pre-fix event leak, then 10 tests passed. Full umbrella mix quality and demo checks passed locally. ExMCP PR #46 remains open; adoption of a fixed release and read-level verification are still required before close. CI: https://github.com/agentjido/jido_connect/actions/runs/34793709535

Connect-side commit 44736e54 passed CI https://github.com/agentjido/jido_connect/actions/runs/34793709535, including umbrella quality, demo, and connector factory. Keep open for ExMCP PR #46 merge/release, fixed dependency adoption, and read-level integration test.

Upstream ExMCP PR #46 merged on 2026-09-16 and issue #42 closed. Master now validates acknowledged notification filters against the requested filter before initial activation and reconnect reads. Hex remains at 1.3.0, which lacks this fix. Connect commit 44736e54 blocks out-of-scope delivery but cannot prevent ExMCP 1.3.0 from making expanded reconnect reads. Keep open until a tagged Hex release is selected and read-level, snapshot, equal/narrower-filter, and reconnect integration checks pass.

Verified on release/3.0 with exact ExMCP Git commit d07c18b0c3f38fa21f65974899d8a9a5047e2dbe (merged PRs #45 and #46). Connect integration test commit 0f2b7981 covers expanded initial acknowledgment rejection, equal/narrower acknowledgment delivery, and expanded reconnect rejection with no resource read or snapshot. Three focused tests passed. Core mix quality: 264 tests, 82.59% coverage. Full umbrella mix quality, demo format/compile/21 tests, and mix hex.audit passed. Connect-side authorized filter guard remains in 44736e54. A fixed Hex release is still required for package publication.
